questions.q: Find the least value of ' $a$ ' so that $f(x)=2 x^2-a x+3$ is an increasing function on $[2,4]$.
questions.solution:
$f(x)=2 x^2-a x+3 \Rightarrow f^{\prime}(x)=4 x-a$
Now $2 \leq x \leq 4 \Rightarrow 8-a \leq 4 x-a \leq 16-a$
For $f$ to be an increasing function, $f^{\prime}(x) \geq 0$
$\Rightarrow 8-a \geq 0 \Rightarrow a \leq 8$
$\therefore$ Least value of a does not exist.

questions.q: If $f(x)=x+\frac{1}{x}, x \geq 1$, show that $f$ is an increasing function.
questions.solution:
$f(x)=x+\frac{1}{x} \Rightarrow f^{\prime}(x)=1-\frac{1}{x^2}=\frac{x^2-1}{x^2}$
Now $\frac{x^2-1}{x^2} \geq 0$ for all $x \geq 1 \Rightarrow f^{\prime}(x) \geq 0 \Rightarrow f$ is an increasing function.

questions.q: The volume of a cube is increasing at the rate of $6 \mathrm{~cm}^3 / \mathrm{s}$. How fast is the surface area of cube increasing, when the length of an edge is 8 cm ?
questions.solution:
Given, $\frac{d V}{d t}=6 \mathrm{~cm}^3 / \mathrm{sec}$. Since, $V=x^3$
$\frac{d V}{d t}=3 x^2 \frac{d x}{d t} \Rightarrow 6=3 x^2 \frac{d x}{d t} \Rightarrow \frac{d x}{d t}=\frac{2}{x^2} \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{sec}$
Now, Surface Area $=\mathrm{S}=6 x^2 \Rightarrow \frac{d S}{d t}=12 x \frac{d x}{d t}=3 \mathrm{~cm}^2 / \mathrm{sec}$

questions.q: The area of the circle is increasing at a uniform rate of $2 \mathrm{~cm}^2 / \mathrm{sec}$. How fast is the circumference of the circle increasing when the radius $r=5 \mathrm{~cm}$ ?

Let $C=2 \pi r$, be the circumference of the circle, $\frac{\mathrm{d}\left(\pi \mathrm{r}^2\right)}{\mathrm{dt}}=2 \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{dr}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\frac{1}{\pi \mathrm{r}} \mathrm{cm} / \mathrm{sec}$
$\frac{\mathrm{dC}}{\mathrm{dt}}=2 \pi \frac{\mathrm{dr}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\frac{2}{\mathrm{r}}=\frac{2}{5} \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{sec}$ at $\mathrm{r}=5 \mathrm{~cm}$

questions.q: Amongst all pairs of positive integers with product as 289 , find which of the two numbers add up to the least.
questions.solution:
Let numbers be ' $x$ ' and ' $y$ ' such that $x y=289 \Rightarrow y=\frac{289}{x}$, ' $S$ ' be their sum, then
$S=x+y=x+\frac{289}{x}$
$\frac{\mathrm{dS}}{\mathrm{dx}}=1-\frac{289}{\mathrm{x}^2}, \frac{\mathrm{dS}}{\mathrm{dx}}=0 \Rightarrow x=17$, a positive integer
$\left.\left.\frac{\mathrm{d}^2 \mathrm{~S}}{\mathrm{dx}^2}\right]_{\mathrm{x}=17}=289\left(\frac{2}{\mathrm{x}^3}\right)\right]_{\mathrm{x}=17}>0, \therefore \mathrm{~S}$ is minimum when $\mathrm{x}=17, \mathrm{y}=17$

A carpenter needs to make a wooden cuboidal box, closed from all sides, which has a square base and fixed volume. Since he is short of the paint required to paint the box on completion, he wants the surface area to be minimum.
On the basis of the above information, answer the following questions :
(i) Taking length $=$ breadth $=\mathrm{x} \mathrm{m}$ and height $=\mathrm{y} \mathrm{m}$, express the surface area (S) of the box in terms of x and its volume (V), which is constant.
(ii) Find $\frac{\mathrm{dS}}{\mathrm{dx}}$.
(iii) (a) Find a relation between x and y such that the surface area (S) is minimum.
(iii) (b) If surface area $(S)$ is constant, the volume $(V)=\frac{1}{4}\left(S x-2 x^3\right)$, $x$ being the edge of base. Show that volume (v) is maximum for $x=\sqrt{\frac{S}{6}}$.
questions.solution:
(i) $\quad V=x^2 y \Rightarrow y=\frac{V}{x^2}$
Hence, $S=2 x^2+4 x y=2 x^2+\frac{4 V}{x}$
(ii) $\frac{\mathrm{dS}}{\mathrm{dx}}=4\left(\mathrm{x}-\frac{\mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{x}^2}\right)$
(iii) (a) $\frac{\mathrm{dS}}{\mathrm{dx}}=\mathbf{0} \Rightarrow \mathrm{V}=\mathrm{x}^3 \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}^2 \mathrm{y}=\mathrm{x}^3 \Rightarrow \mathrm{y}=x$
$\frac{d^2 s}{d x^2}=4\left(1+\frac{2 V}{x^3}\right)>0 \Rightarrow S$ is minimum if $y=x$.
(iii) (b)
$V=\frac{1}{4}\left(S x-2 x^3\right) \Rightarrow \frac{d V}{d x}=\frac{1}{4}\left(S-6 x^2\right)$
Put $\frac{d V}{d x}=0 \Rightarrow x=\sqrt{\frac{S}{6}}$
$\left(\frac{d^2 v}{d x^2}\right)_{x=\sqrt{\frac{s}{6}}}=-3 \sqrt{\frac{s}{6}}<0 \Rightarrow$ Volume is maximum for $x=\sqrt{\frac{s}{6}}$.

questions.q:
A store has been selling calculators at ₹ 350 each. A market survey indicates that a reduction in price (p) of calculator increases the number of units $(x)$ sold. The relation between the price and quantity sold is given by the demand function $\mathrm{p}=450-\frac{1}{2} x$.

Based on the above information, answer the following questions :
(i) Determine the number of units ($x$) that should be sold to maximise the revenue $\mathrm{R}(x)=x \mathrm{p}(x)$. Also, verify the result.
(ii) What rebate in price of calculator should the store give to maximise the revenue?
questions.solution:
(i) Revenue by selling $x$ items $=R(x)=x \cdot p(x)=450 x-\frac{x^2}{2} \frac{d R}{d x}=450-x$
For Maxima or Minima, $\frac{d R}{d x}=0 \Rightarrow x=450$
$\frac{d^2 R}{d x^2}=-1<0$
(Revenue is maximum when $x=450$ units are sold)
(ii) At $x=450, p=450-\frac{450}{2}=225$
So, Rebate $=350-225=$ Rs. 125 per calculator

questions.q:
A rectangular visiting card is to contain 24 sq.cm. of printed matter. The margins at the top and bottom of the card are to be 1 cm and the margins on the left and right are to be $11 / 2 \mathrm{~cm}$ as shown below :

On the basis of the above information, answer the following questions :

(ii) Obtain the dimensions of the card of minimum area.
questions.solution:
(i) Let $\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{x})$ be the area of the visiting card then,
As $\mathrm{xy}=24, \mathrm{~A}(\mathrm{x})=(\mathrm{x}+3)(\mathrm{y}+2)=2 \mathrm{x}+3 \mathrm{y}+\mathrm{xy}+6=2 \mathrm{x}+\frac{72}{\mathrm{x}}+30$
(ii) $\mathrm{A}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=2-\frac{72}{\mathrm{x}^2}$ and $\mathrm{A}^{\prime \prime}(\mathrm{x})=\frac{144}{\mathrm{x}^3}$,
solving $A^{\prime}(x)=0 \Rightarrow x=6$ is the critical point.
$\mathrm{A}^{\prime \prime}(6)=\frac{144}{6}>0, \therefore$ Area of the card is minimum at $x=6, y=4$
The dimension of the card with minimum area is Length $=9 \mathrm{~cm}$, Breadth $=6 \mathrm{~cm}$

questions.q:
The use of electric vehicles will curb air pollution in the long run.

The use of electric vehicles is increasing every year and estimated electric vehicles in use at any time t is given by the function V :
$\mathrm{V}(\mathrm{t})=\frac{1}{5} \mathrm{t}^3-\frac{5}{2} \mathrm{t}^2+25 \mathrm{t}-2$
where t represents the time and $\mathrm{t}=1,2,3 \ldots$ corresponds to year 2001, 2002, 2003, $\_\_\_\_$ respectively.
Based on the above information, answer the following questions :
(i) Can the above function be used to estimate number of vehicles in the year 2000 ? Justify.
(ii) Prove that the function $\mathrm{V}(\mathrm{t})$ is an increasing function.
questions.solution:
(i) For the year $2000, t=0 \& V(0)=-2$ and the number of vehicles cannot be negative
$\therefore$ the given function $V(t)$ cannot be used.
(ii) $\mathrm{V}^{\prime}(\mathrm{t})=\frac{3}{5} \mathrm{t}^2-5 \mathrm{t}+25=\frac{3}{5}\left[\left(\mathrm{t}-\frac{25}{6}\right)^2+\frac{875}{36}\right]>0, \therefore \mathrm{~V}(\mathrm{t})$ is an increasing function.

questions.q:
Engine displacement is the measure of the cylinder volume swept by all the pistons of a piston engine. The piston moves inside the cylinder bore

The cylinder bore in the form of circular cylinder open at the top is to be made from a metal sheet of area $75 \pi \mathrm{~cm}^2$.
Based on the above information, answer the following questions :
(i) If the radius of cylinder is r cm and height is h cm, then write the volume $V$ of cylinder in terms of radius $r$.
(ii) Find $\frac{\mathrm{dV}}{\mathrm{dr}}$.
(iii) (a) Find the radius of cylinder when its volume is maximum.
(iii)(b) For maximum volume, $h>r$. State true or false and justify.
questions.solution:
(i) $\pi r^2+2 \pi r h=75 \pi \Rightarrow h=\frac{75-r^2}{2 r}, \therefore V=\pi r^2 h=\frac{\pi}{2}\left(75 r-r^3\right)$
(ii) $\frac{\mathrm{dV}}{\mathrm{dr}}=\frac{\pi}{2}\left(75-3 \mathrm{r}^2\right)$
(iii) $\left.\frac{d V}{d r}=0 \Rightarrow r=5, \frac{d^2 V}{d r^2}\right]_{r=5}=\frac{\pi}{2}(-6 r)<0 \therefore$ volume is maximum when $r=5$
(iii)(b)
False, $\left.\frac{d V}{d r}=0 \Rightarrow r=5, \frac{d^2 V}{d r^2}\right]_{r=5}=\frac{\pi}{2}(-6 r)<0 \therefore$ volume is maximum when $r=5$ As volume is maximum at $r=5 \Rightarrow h=\frac{75-5^2}{2(5)}=5 \Rightarrow h=r$

questions.q:
In order to set up a rain water harvesting system, a tank to collect rain water is to be dug. The tank should have a square base and a capacity of $250 \mathrm{~m}^3$. The cost of land is ₹ 5,000 per square metre and cost of digging increases with depth and for the whole tank, it is ₹ $40,000 \mathrm{~h}^2$, where h is the depth of the tank in metres. $x$ is the side of the square base of the tank in metres.
ELEMENTS OF A TYPICAL RAIN WATER HARVESTING SYSTEM

Based on the above information, answer the following questions :
(i) Find the total cost C of digging the tank in terms of x.
(ii) Find $\frac{\mathrm{dC}}{\mathrm{dx}}$.
(iii) (a) Find the value of x for which cost C is minimum.
(iii)(b) Check whether the cost function $C(x)$ expressed in terms of $x$ is increasing or not, where $\mathrm{x}>0$.

questions.q: An open tank with a square base and vertical sides is to be constructed from a metal sheet so as to hold a given quantity of water. Show that the cost of material will be least when depth of the tank is half of its width. If the cost is to be borne by nearby settled lower income families, for whom water will be provided, what kind of value is hidden in this question?
questions.solution:
Let side of base $=x$ and depth of tank $=y$
$V=x^2 y \Rightarrow y=\frac{V}{x^2},(V=$ Quantity of water $=$ constant $)$
Cost of material is least when area of sheet used is minimum.
$A($ Surface area of tank $)=x^2+4 x y=x^2+\frac{4 V}{x}$
$\frac{d A}{d x}=2 x-\frac{4 V}{x^2}, \frac{d A}{d x}=0 \Rightarrow x^3=2 V, y=\frac{x^3}{2 x^2}=\frac{x}{2}$
$\frac{d^2 A}{d x^2}=2+\frac{8 V}{x^3}>0, \quad \therefore$ Area is minimum, thus cost is minimum when $y=\frac{x}{2}$
Value: Any relevant value.

questions.q:
The relation between the height of the plant $(y \mathrm{~cm})$ with respect to exposure to sunlight is governed by the equation $y=4 x-\frac{1}{2} x^2$, where $x$ is the number of days exposed to sunlight.
(i) Find the rate of growth of the plant with respect to sunlight.
(ii) In how many days will the plant attain its maximum height ? What is the maximum height?
questions.solution:
(i) $y=4 x-\frac{1}{2} x^2 \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}=(4-x) \mathrm{cm} /$ day
(ii) For maximum height, $\frac{d y}{d x}=0 \Rightarrow x=4$ days as $\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}<0$, number of days $=4$
Now, Maximum height $=y(4)=16-\frac{1}{2}(16)=8 \mathrm{~cm}$

questions.q: The median of an equilateral triangle is increasing at the rate of $2 \sqrt{3} \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$. Find the rate at which its side is increasing.
questions.solution:
In an equilateral triangle, median is same as altitude. Let ' $h$ ' denote the length of the median (or altitude) and ' $x$ ' be the side of $\triangle \mathrm{ABC}$.

Then, $h=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} x$ or $x=\frac{2 h}{\sqrt{3}}\_\_\_\_$ (i)
It is given that $\frac{\mathrm{dh}}{\mathrm{dt}}=2 \sqrt{3} \quad$ So, by (i) we have
$\frac{d x}{d t}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \frac{d h}{d t} \Rightarrow \frac{d x}{d t}=4$
Thus, the side of $\Delta \mathrm{ABC}$ is increasing at the rate of $4 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{sec}$.

questions.q: Find the dimensions of the rectangle of perimeter 36 cm which will sweep out a volume as large as possible, when revolved about one of its side. Also, find the maximum volume.
questions.solution:
Let sides of a rectangle are $x \mathrm{~cm}$ and $y \mathrm{~cm}$.
Given $2 x+2 y=36 \Rightarrow y=18-x$
Volume, $V=\pi x^2 y=\pi x^2(18-x)=\pi\left(18 x^2-x^3\right)$
$\Rightarrow \frac{d V}{d x}=\pi\left(36 x-3 x^2\right)$
For maxima/minima, put $\frac{d V}{d x}=0$
$\Rightarrow x=12 \mathrm{~cm}(\because x
eq 0)$
Again, $\frac{d^2 V}{d x^2}=\pi(36-6 x)$
$\left.\Rightarrow \frac{d^2 V}{d x^2}\right|_{x=12 \mathrm{~cm}}=-36 \pi<0$
$\therefore$ Volume is maximum when $x=12 \mathrm{~cm}$.
Also, $y=(18-x) \mathrm{cm}=6 \mathrm{~cm}$
Dimension of rectangle are $12 \mathrm{~cm} \times 6 \mathrm{~cm}$
$\text { Maximum volume }=\pi x^2 y=864 \pi \mathrm{~cm}^3$

questions.q: Show that the height of the cylinder of maximum volume that can be inscribed in a sphere of radius $R$ is $\frac{2 R}{\sqrt{3}}$. Also find the maximum volume.
questions.solution:
In rt. $\triangle \mathrm{ABC} ; 4 \mathrm{x}^2+\mathrm{h}^2=4 \mathrm{R}^2, \mathrm{x}^2=\frac{4 \mathrm{R}^2-\mathrm{h}^2}{4}$
$\mathrm{V}($ Volume of cylinder $)=\pi \mathrm{x}^2 \mathrm{~h}=\frac{\pi}{4}\left(4 \mathrm{R}^2 \mathrm{~h}-\mathrm{h}^3\right)$
$\mathrm{V}^{\prime}(\mathrm{h})=\frac{\pi}{4}\left(4 \mathrm{R}^2-3 \mathrm{~h}^2\right) ; \mathrm{V}^{\prime \prime}(\mathrm{h})=\frac{\pi}{4}(-6 \mathrm{~h})$
$\mathrm{V}^{\prime}(\mathrm{h})=0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{~h}=\frac{2 \mathrm{R}}{\sqrt{3}}$
$\mathrm{V}^{\prime \prime}\left(\frac{2 \mathrm{R}}{\sqrt{3}}\right)=\frac{-6 \pi}{4}\left(\frac{2 \mathrm{R}}{\sqrt{3}}\right)<0 \Rightarrow$ Volume ' V ' is max.
$\text { for } h=\frac{2 R}{\sqrt{3}}$
Max. Volume: $V=\frac{4}{3 \sqrt{3}} \pi R^3$
